signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Tightening Repricing
signals.text: The G10 scorecard highlights JPY as the weekly outperformer averaging +1.777% across 7 pairs, while SEK anchors the laggard end at −1.461% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 3.238% bilateral spread. Headwinds for SEK mount following Sweden's subdued inflation profile alongside a negative ESI reading of −6.7, contrasting with Japan's ESI running at +23.8. JPY speculative positioning shows an unprecedented covering impulse of +58,042 contracts WoW to leave net short at −53,255, driven by market expectations that the Bank of Japan will hike its policy rate to 1.25% at its upcoming policy meeting. While the nominal BoJ rate of 1.0% vs Riksbank at 1.75% still represents a carry deficit, real policy rate differentials and massive short-covering flows drive the bilateral gap. Trade bias: Long JPY/SEK, theme-driven policy divergence and short covering. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate decision. Risk: BoJ holds rates at 1.0% with dovish forward guidance, unwinding yen gains.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.78, holding well below its SMA20 at 157.62, SMA50 at 159.69, and SMA200 at 158.41. FX options pricing reflects acute downside demand with the 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversal printing at −2.09 (Saxo Bank, 1M tenor, indicative mid), marking a severe put skew even as VIX sits at 15.8 (normal volatility). In sharp contrast, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment is positioned 85% long against 15% short, establishing an extreme retail-long posture that diverges directly from institutional downside protection flows. Although Fed SOFR at 3.62% vs BoJ TONA at 0.98% maintains a +264bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, market repricing ahead of the BoJ decision forces aggressive downside hedging. Trade bias: Short USD/JPY, positioning squeeze against retail long. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — rate decision. Risk: Sustained close above the SMA200 at 158.41 invalidating the short structure.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7162, holding above its SMA20 at 0.7168, SMA50 at 0.7069, and SMA200 at 0.7003. CFTC Leveraged Funds net positioning sits long at +48,379 contracts, placing positioning at the 93rd percentile and a z-score of +1.72 over its 52-week history, indicating upper-decile institutional crowding. Flow has begun to stall with Leveraged Funds shedding −1,871 contracts WoW while price consolidates just under recent highs. RBA cash rate at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% provides a +60bp nominal carry advantage (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.62% provides −73bp favoring AUD), yet the 25d Risk Reversal at −0.67 reflects a protective put skew that signals caution into the rally. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; crowded positioning caps near-term upside. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — rate decision. Risk: A daily close below the SMA20 at 0.7168 triggering speculative long liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Inflation Shock + Technical Anchor
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1593, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1630 and SMA200 at 1.1637 while holding above its SMA50 at 1.1532. Fed SOFR at 3.62% vs ECB €STR at 2.19% generates favoring USD (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.65% — 110bp nominal spread), structurally capping euro rallies. However, ECB President Lagarde's remarks indicating that the euro-area inflation shock will endure longer than anticipated reinforce policy sensitivity into upcoming meetings. Leveraged Funds positioning reflects this conflict, trimming net short exposure by +6,403 contracts WoW to −46,381 (pctl 34, z −0.25). Trade bias: Neutral/short EUR/USD; carry advantage favors USD into resistance. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde Speech 15:15 UTC. Risk: A clean break and daily close above the SMA200 at 1.1637 negating dollar carry dominance.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Negative Vol Risk Premium
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8169, maintaining levels above its SMA20 at 0.8074, SMA50 at 0.8093, and SMA200 at 0.7934. Options volatility displays an atypical negative risk premium, with 1-month ATM implied volatility at 6.8% trading 0.6 percentage points below the 30-day realized volatility of 7.4% (VRP −0.6%). This pricing compression occurs despite Fed SOFR at 3.62% vs SNB SARON at −0.04% yielding a substantial +366bp carry advantage favoring the dollar (Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.0% — +375bp nominal carry). Leveraged Funds remain net short CHF at −13,968 contracts (pctl 12, z −1.09), showing low market appetite for buying franc downside protection. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF; carry premium intact while options volatility remains compressed. Catalyst: SNB meeting 24 Sep — rate decision. Risk: Break below the SMA50 support at 0.8093 accompanied by a sharp spike in front-month implied volatility.
